An RPG reminiscent of the Final Fantasy series, Octopath Traveler pairs modern graphics with a wonderfully cozy style. While the story doesn’t quite match FF's depth, the engaging combat system, gorgeous art style, and brilliant soundtrack easily make up for it. As someone who deeply values a game's aesthetic, I highly recommend it. An extra bonus: despite its updated visuals, it remains remarkably lightweight, requiring minimal storage and resources.

The only thing I’d change is making it easier to play in the background. Currently, the mouse gets trapped inside the window (even in windowed mode) requiring a press of the Windows key to free it.

Pretty much perfect as what it's meant to be. Everything from the graphics, to the mechanics are all an homage to snes era JRPGs in a way that highlights it rather than replicates it perfectly. It also imports shortcomings from that era, but not to a hugely detrimental degree and I think their inclusion was intentional as part of recreating the genre.

The only full negative is the game's length could make in inaccessible for some. The intro is longer than most games.

As a longtime fan of the Final Fantasy Series, i had been searching for games that capture the special feeling the early games had. This game does so beautifully. The soundtrack, impeccable. The stories, interesting, disturbing, diverse. And the combat... ooooohhh man. The combat system is engaging, giving various ways to handle the game. Do you focus on breaking enemies guard as many times as possible for a turn advantage? Or do you set everything up to cash in for one huge burst of damage? I will be recommending this game to everyone I know for a long, long time.

This game isn't worth the price tag at all. The main story lines are all rather short and easy to beat. After that the late game is comprised of optional quests. Sure this game has strategy elements, but now that I have been in the late game, it feels like RNG is equally important. I caved and looked up strategies,

Combat is stellar, some of the best I've seen from a JRPG.

The reason I can't recommend this is the narrative, or lack thereof. Before people start, I know there's the whole Gate of Finis section, but locking the 'proper' story behind eight mediocre storylines, a bunch of seemingly random side quests, 50+ hours of content, and an absurdly difficult boss rush isn't quite cutting it, imo.

It's not just the lack of depth to the characters, but also the strange way they handle the travelling aspect. Most of the time, the other travellers aren't acknowledged. Each traveller is seemingly alone on their journey, which would be fine IF they didn't randomly start acknowledging each other in traveller banter. It's so damn weird. Like, pick a lane.
♥♥♥♥ purple chests and the talent to pick locks not being tied to the thief job.

I have over 100 hours in Octopath Traveler, and I honestly find it difficult to recommend it.

Before I explain why, let me start with who I do recommend it to.

If you've already played a lot of mainstream JRPGs and are curious to see where Square Enix's HD-2D style began, I think it's worth checking out.

Who wouldn't I recommend it to? Anyone who cares a lot about storytelling, anyone who is still new to JRPGs since there are many better games that deserve your time first, and anyone who gets annoyed by repetitive music. I'll come back to that later.

I just installed a mod to speed up combat, and I wish I had done it from the start. The early stories are pretty bare bones, and the characters feel pretty one note. I've heard the story gets better later on, but I'm close to 50 hours in: that's a long time to wait personally. 

The nostalgic graphics are done well.
